extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary criticism; writers and critics considering the qualities of 'Men of Letters' and literary greatness
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and virtues by which 18th–19th-century 'Men of Letters' (writers, poets, intellectuals) are judged: sincerity, belief, strength, originality, moral prudence, restraint, and related qualities illustrated by Johnson, Rousseau, Burns, etc. Useful for critics, biographers, or anyone assessing literary character and achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity / heart-sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: The sincere man speaks from the heart of Nature; sincerity is the primary material of great writers ('heart-sincerity', 'he stands by truth, speaks by it, works and lives by it').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Johnson is praised for 'sincerity' even within an artificial dialect; anti-patterns include cant, affectation, and insincere 'simulacra' that substitute performance for real feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belief as the basis for action
rubrics_metrics.description: Belief is 'the healthy act of a man's mind' and necessary for genuine action — one must get to belief rather than live in perpetual debate or displayed doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish permissible doubt/inquiry from chronic scepticism; avoid parading doubt as a virtue. A writer must have convictions that enable work and heroism rather than endless sceptical paralysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality understood as genuineness (not mere novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality is not simply 'that it be new' but being genuine and rooted in truth; 'the essence of originality is not that it be new' but that it be true to nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulas and traditional paths are legitimate when they embody substance; improvement and widening of a path is preferred to novelty-for-its-own-sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength as calm endurance (not vehemence)
rubrics_metrics.description: True strength is calm force and the ability to 'walk under the heaviest weight without staggering' rather than convulsive vehemence or spasmodic intensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Rousseau's 'vehemence and rigidity' mistaken for strength; value steadiness, sustained labor, and capacity for hardship over spectacular outbursts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnestness / being 'in earnest'
rubrics_metrics.description: Great men are 'heartily in earnest'; earnestness (deep commitment and seriousness) is a chief mark of a heroic writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rousseau is credited with earnestness even where other virtues fail; earnest feeling is necessary but not sufficient without restraint and strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint and the 'talent of silence'
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuable talent is the ability to hold silence until the right time — 'to consume his own smoke' and not emit undigested ideas prematurely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: constant outspoken convulsion that produces 'smoke' rather than 'fire' (coherent, tested work). Cultivate patience and internal refinement before public utterance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral prudence and practical action
rubrics_metrics.description: A moral prudence that prioritizes 'how you will do it' in a world with much to do and little to know; clear your mind of cant and act effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preach practicality: avoid windy sentimentalism and empty moralizing. The 'Gospel' of Johnson is to act wisely in the face of limited knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over style; meaningful formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulas and stylistic forms are not bad in themselves but must be 'full of substance'; avoid beautiful styles with 'nothing in them'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept traditional forms when they carry genuine content; condemn works that are merely ornamental or rhetorically flashy without real thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of egoism and appetite for praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Egoism — vanity and hunger for the praise of men — is the source of many faults and miseries and diminishes true heroism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate humility and victory over mere desire; Rousseau's failures are attributed in part to egoism. Anti-pattern: producing work primarily to feed vanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity vs quackery and simulacra
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuine acting and authentic creation are opposed to quackery, mimicry, and 'similitude of acting' that substitutes appearance for real work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware eras or authors that favor performance and plausibility over truth; value real labor and authentic contribution rather than theatrical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing on one's own basis / self-reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers should 'stand on our own basis' — accept the hard reality they can honestly attain rather than begging or borrowing another's forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration: Johnson's pride in honest self-help (pitching away the gifted shoes). Encourage integrity and self-respect over dependency or pretension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellect as qualification for governance (men of letters in public office)
rubrics_metrics.description: The suggestion that men of talent should be tried as governors: intellectual capacity ('Understanding') is a fundamental qualification for administration and worth testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given of Chinese practice of advancing talented youths; guidance: try intellectuals in governance even if inexperienced at administration, because understanding is indispensable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition through ordeal / meritocratic struggle
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuine merit (the Burns who merits support) must pass through the ordeal of 'Literary Life' — struggle and test are the legitimate means of recognizing talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: leaving recognition to blind chance leads to waste; while social mechanisms may improve recognition, the ordeal of struggle produces strong men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, solidity, and method (exemplified in reference work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works (e.g., Johnson's Dictionary) should display 'clearness of definition, general solidity, honesty, insight and successful method' — an 'architectural nobleness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value careful method, precise definition, structural completeness in scholarly or reference work over rhetorical flourish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belief versus scepticism; the necessity of faith for heroism
rubrics_metrics.description: Scepticism produces 'spiritual paralysis' and an age of simulacra; a return to sincere belief (faith) restores possibility for heroism and genuine work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnosis: the 18th-century sceptical world degraded truth to plausibility. Remedy: cultivate sincerity and belief; avoid mechanical atheism and mere 'doctrine of motives' that reduce action to self-interest.
